checks: Source 68d3d3976d28a947:03 §§1–2 uses the same determinant-one axial stretch, common transverse body and own-centroid normalization. Integration of section powers gives V and the two axial centroids. The transverse centroid vanishes because g_Q=0.

The simultaneous proper interval comes from intersecting −1/(d+1)<s<a and −ka<s<k/(d+1); k≥1 and d≥2 make the first lower endpoint the larger. The stationarity relation is (a+s/k)=t(a−s) with t^(d−1)=k. The second power base is <1 by t^d−dt+d+1≥2, and the first is positive. Convexity gives its minimum. Outside, on the left the first is full; on the right the second is full or the first is empty with a nondecreasing second tail. The zero-shift cost is at most one.

For a fixed summed axial coordinate x, the radius sum decreases faster with the allocation to A than with the allocation to D. Maximizing by first filling the D coordinate gives the displayed two pieces. All sections are nonnegative multiples of the same convex Q containing zero, so the largest contains the other possible sections. Integration gives (k/ρ)[(1+ρ)^d−1]+1=1+(1+t)^d−t^d in units V before averaging.

At t=1 both numerator and its derivative vanish, while the relative excess derivative is d(2^(d−1)−1)/2^d. For t>1 the stationary shift is strictly positive and improves the zero shift, and the denominator is positive and increasing. Bounded numerator and diverging denominator give limit zero at infinity. The strictly positive ratio therefore attains a maximum in the interior.
For d=2 the ratio simplifies to (8/9)(k−1)/(k²+1). Its derivative is proportional to 2−(k−1)². Substituting k=1+√2 gives 4(√2−1)/9, and k=2 gives the exact triple (4/5,1/2,8/45).

overlap.comparison: Covers the identical-body k=1 case but not the distinct equal-volume cone pair with k>1.
Uses homothetic body scales with weights r^d,s^d. Here the affine stretch has determinant one, so both weights are one and the exact midpoint excess is separate.
A finite universal linear coefficient fails for another family. The coefficient here is optimized only for axial cuts in these volume-preserving cone pairs.
